After further threats they let them go. They could not find a way to punish them, because all the people were glorifying God for what had happened.

notes.note: If it would be helpful in your language, you could express this with an active form. Alternate translation: [felt ashamed]

notes.quote: τοῖς ἐνδόξοις τοῖς γινομένοις ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ
notes.note: If it would be helpful in your language, you could express this with an active form. Alternate translation: [the glorious things Jesus was doing]

verses.text: Then Jesus asked, “What is the kingdom of God like? To what can I compare it?

xrefs.text: Then He asked, “To what can we compare the kingdom of God? With what parable shall we present it?
Nor will people say, ‘Look, here it is, or ‘There it is. For you see, the kingdom of God is in your midst.
He put before them another parable: “The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed that a man took and planted in his field.
Jesus also said, “The kingdom of God is like a man who scatters seed on the ground.
Again He asked, “To what can I compare the kingdom of God?
Jesus put before them another parable: “The kingdom of heaven is like a man who sowed good seed in his field.
“To what, then, can I compare the men of this generation? What are they like?

What can I say for you? To what can I compare you, O Daughter of Jerusalem? To what can I liken you, that I may console you, O Virgin Daughter of Zion? For your wound is as deep as the sea. Who can ever heal you?

notes.quote: τίνι ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ Βασιλεία τοῦ Θεοῦ, καὶ τίνι ὁμοιώσω αὐτήν
notes.note: These two questions mean basically the same thing. Jesus uses the repetition to catch the attention of his audience. If it would be helpful in your language, you could combine the questions, especially if it might be confusing for your readers if you put both of them in. Alternate translation: [What example can I use to show you what the kingdom of God is like]

notes.quote: τίνι ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ Βασιλεία τοῦ Θεοῦ, καὶ τίνι ὁμοιώσω αὐτήν
notes.note: Jesus is using the question form as teaching tool. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate his words as a statement. It may be helpful to make this two sentences. Alternate translation: [I want to tell you what the kingdom of God is like. I am going to compare it with something.]

notes.quote: τίνι ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ Βασιλεία τοῦ Θεοῦ
notes.note: See how you decided to translate the phrase the kingdom of God in 4:43. If it would be helpful in your language, you could express the idea behind the abstract noun kingdom with a verb such as “rule.” Alternate translation: [What is it like when God rules]

verses.text: It is like a mustard seed that a man tossed into his garden. It grew and became a tree, and the birds of the air nested in its branches.

xrefs.text: Its leaves were beautiful, its fruit was abundant, and upon it was food for all. Under it the beasts of the field found shelter, in its branches the birds of the air nested, and from it every creature was fed.

In the days of those kings, the God of heaven will set up a kingdom that will never be destroyed, nor will it be left to another people. It will shatter all these kingdoms and bring them to an end, but will itself stand forever.
whose foliage was beautiful and whose fruit was abundant, providing food for all, under which the beasts of the field lived, and in whose branches the birds of the air nested—

This is what the Lord GOD says: ‘I will take a shoot from the lofty top of the cedar, and I will set it out. I will pluck a tender sprig from its topmost shoots, and I will plant it on a high and lofty mountain.
He put before them another parable: “The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed that a man took and planted in his field.
“On that day many nations will join themselves to the LORD, and they will become My people. I will dwell among you, and you will know that the LORD of Hosts has sent Me to you.
It is like a mustard seed, which is the smallest of all seeds sown upon the earth.
It will be a unique day known only to the LORD, without day or night; but when evening comes, there will be light.

notes.note: This is a simile or comparison. Alternate translation: [The kingdom of God is like a mustard seed]

This comparison is also a parable, a brief illustration designed to help the people understand what Jesus is teaching. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could state that explicitly in your translation. Alternate translation: [Then Jesus gave the people in the synagogue this illustration to help them understand. “The kingdom of God is like a mustard seed]

A mustard seed is a very small seed that grows into a large plant. If your readers would not be familiar with it, in your translation you could use the name of another seed like it, or you could use a general phrase. Alternate translation: [a very small seed]

This could: (1) be a generic sense that includes all people. Alternate translation: [a person]; (2) refers to a man and a woman in paired examples to offer a comprehensive teaching about the kingdom of God, since Jesus speaks in his next illustration of a woman doing something. In that case, it would be appropriate to say a man here.

In this culture, people planted some kinds of seeds by throwing them so that they scattered in a garden. Jesus assumes that his listeners will know this. Alternate translation: [and planted in his garden]

notes.quote: τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ κατεσκήνωσεν ἐν τοῖς κλάδοις αὐτοῦ
notes.note: In your language, it might seem that this phrase expresses unnecessary extra information. If so, you could abbreviate it. However, you could also use an action clause to keep the sense of “sky.” Alternate translation: [birds built their nests in its branches] or [birds flew down and made nests in its branches]

verses.text: Again He asked, “To what can I compare the kingdom of God?

notes.quote: τίνι ὁμοιώσω τὴν Βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ
notes.note: Jesus once again uses a question as a teaching tool. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate his words as a statement. Alternate translation: [I am going to compare the kingdom of God to something else.]

notes.quote: τίνι ὁμοιώσω τὴν Βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ
notes.note: See how you decided to translate the phrase the kingdom of God in 4:43. If it would be helpful in your language, you could express the idea behind the abstract noun kingdom with a verb such as “rule.” Alternate translation: [I am going to use another comparison to show you what is it like when God rules.]

verses.text: It is like leaven that a woman took and mixed into three measures of flour, until all of it was leavened.

being confident of this, that He who began a good work in you will carry it on to completion until the day of Christ Jesus.

He cuts off every branch in Me that bears no fruit, and every branch that does bear fruit, He prunes to make it even more fruitful.
And this is my prayer: that your love may abound more and more in knowledge and depth of insight,

notes.note: This is a simile or comparison. Alternate translation: [The kingdom of God is like yeast]

This comparison is also a parable, a brief illustration designed to help the crowds understand what Jesus is teaching. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could state that explicitly in your translation. Alternate translation: [Then Jesus gave them this further illustration to help them understand. “The kingdom of God is like yeast]
See how you translated yeast in 12:1. Alternate translation: [leaven]

Jesus assumes that his listeners will know that only a little bit of yeast is needed to make a lot of dough rise. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could state that explicitly. Alternate translation: [a little bit of yeast]

The term seahs is the plural of “seah,” a dry measure equivalent to nearly eight liters or two gallons. You can express this quantity in terms of a measure that your culture uses, or you can use a general expression. Alternate translation: [a large amount of flour]
If it would be helpful in your language, you could express this with an active form. Alternate translation: [the yeast caused all of it to rise]

how God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Spirit and with power, and how Jesus went around doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil, because God was with Him.

verses.text: “Lord, someone asked Him, “will only a few people be saved? Jesus answered,

notes.note: Luke uses this phrase to introduce a new character into the story. Alternate translation: [someone in one of those places asked him]

If it would be helpful in your language, you could express this with an active form, and you could state who would do the action. Alternate translation: [is God going to save only a few people?]

The implication is that a crowd had gathered to meet Jesus as he went through this place on his journey, and that the questioner was one person in the crowd. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could state that explicitly. Alternate translation: [Jesus replied to this person and to the whole crowd that was there]

named.name: LORD

verses.text: “Make every effort to enter through the narrow door. For many, I tell you, will try to enter and will not be able.

xrefs.text: Enter through the narrow gate. For wide is the gate and broad is the way that leads to destruction, and many enter through it.
Therefore, brothers, strive to make your calling and election sure. For if you practice these things you will never stumble,
Do you not know that in a race all the runners run, but only one receives the prize? Run in such a way as to take the prize.
Let us, therefore, make every effort to enter that rest, so that no one will fall by following the same pattern of disobedience.
So keep watch at all times, and pray that you may have the strength to escape all that is about to happen and to stand before the Son of Man.
So My people come to you as usual, sit before you, and hear your words; but they do not put them into practice. Although they express love with their mouths, their hearts pursue dishonest gain.
Therefore, my beloved, just as you have always obeyed, not only in my presence, but now even more in my absence, continue to work out your salvation with fear and trembling.
The craving of the slacker kills him because his hands refuse to work.

notes.quote: ἀγωνίζεσθε εἰσελθεῖν διὰ τῆς στενῆς θύρας
notes.note: Jesus is speaking about God’s kingdom as if people had to go through a small doorway with great difficulty to enter it. Alternate translation: [Work hard to overcome every difficulty that would keep you from entering God’s kingdom]
Jesus says this to emphasize what he is telling the crowd. Alternate translation: [you must understand]
Even though Jesus is answering an individual’s question, he is talking to the whole crowd, so the word you is plural. The implied you in the command to struggle earlier in this verse is also plural.

notes.quote: πολλοί & ζητήσουσιν εἰσελθεῖν καὶ οὐκ ἰσχύσουσιν
notes.note: The implication is that they will not be able to enter because it is so difficult. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could state that explicitly. Alternate translation: [many of the people who try to enter the kingdom of God … will not be able to, because it is so difficult]

verses.text: After the master of the house gets up and shuts the door, you will stand outside knocking and saying, ‘Lord, open the door for us. But he will reply, ‘I do not know where you are from.

xrefs.text: But while they were on their way to buy it, the bridegroom arrived. Those who were ready went in with him to the wedding banquet, and the door was shut.
And he will answer, ‘I tell you, I do not know where you are from. Depart from me, all you evildoers.
Not everyone who says to Me, ‘Lord, Lord, will enter the kingdom of heaven, but only he who does the will of My Father in heaven.
Why do you call Me ‘Lord, Lord, but do not do what I say?
Seek the LORD while He may be found; call on Him while He is near.
For He says: “In the time of favor I heard you, and in the day of salvation I helped you.” Behold, now is the time of favor; now is the day of salvation!
Then He will say to those on His left, ‘Depart from Me, you who are cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels.
For you know that afterward, when he wanted to inherit the blessing, he was rejected. He could find no ground for repentance, though he sought the blessing with tears.

notes.quote: ἀφ’ οὗ ἂν ἐγερθῇ ὁ οἰκοδεσπότης καὶ ἀποκλείσῃ τὴν θύραν
notes.note: Jesus extends the metaphor of the door by speaking of God at the time of final judgment as if God were the owner of a house and the people he is addressing were outside the house trying to get in. Alternate translation: [After God has admitted everyone who is going to enter his kingdom and is not letting anyone else in]
Even though Jesus is answering an individual’s question, he is talking to the whole crowd, so the word you is plural in all of these cases.

notes.quote: κρούειν τὴν θύραν λέγοντες, κύριε, ἄνοιξον ἡμῖν
notes.note: If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [knock on the door and ask the Lord to open it for you]
See how you translated the word “knock” in 11:9. Alternate translation: [call out] or [cough] or [clap]
The people knocking on the door mean themselves but not the owner of the house, so if your language distinguishes between exclusive and inclusive us, use the exclusive form here.
Together the two words answer and say mean that the owner of the house will respond to the people who are knocking on the door. Alternate translation: [he will respond]

notes.quote: ἀποκριθεὶς ἐρεῖ ὑμῖν, οὐκ οἶδα ὑμᾶς, πόθεν ἐστέ
notes.note: If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [he will respond that he does not know you or where you are from]

The owner is speaking in an abbreviated way. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could draw on the first phrase to supply the words that are missing from the second phrase, as UST does. Alternate translation: [I do not know you, and I do not know where you are from]

The owner is also using repetition for emphasis. If this would not be clear in your language and your readers might wonder why he was saying the same thing twice, you could translate this with a single phrase that expresses the basic meaning. Alternate translation: [I do not know who you are]

verses.text: Then you will say, ‘We ate and drank with you, and you taught in our streets.

xrefs.text: They profess to know God, but by their actions they deny Him. They are detestable, disobedient, and unfit for any good deed.

For day after day they seek Me and delight to know My ways, like a nation that does what is right and does not forsake the justice of their God. They ask Me for righteous judgments; they delight in the nearness of God.”
having a form of godliness but denying its power. Turn away from such as these!

notes.quote: ἄρξεσθε λέγειν, ἐφάγομεν ἐνώπιόν σου καὶ ἐπίομεν, καὶ ἐν ταῖς πλατείαις ἡμῶν ἐδίδαξας
notes.note: If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [you will begin to tell him that you shared meals with him and he taught in the streets of your town]
Here, before means “in the presence” of another person. Alternate translation: [You were with us when we ate and drank] or [We ate and drank together with you]
The people are using the two components of a meal to mean an entire meal. Alternate translation: [We shared meals]
Since the people are addressing the owner alone, the pronoun you would be singular here, and also in any case where it is needed in your language as a pronoun for a verb, for example, you taught.

Within the extended metaphor, the people are addressing Jesus, who was not from their town, but who taught them as he traveled through. So the people would consider the streets to be theirs but not his, and our would be exclusive, if your language marks that distinction.

verses.text: And he will answer, ‘I tell you, I do not know where you are from. Depart from me, all you evildoers.

xrefs.text: Depart from me, all you workers of iniquity, for the LORD has heard my weeping.

Nevertheless, God’s firm foundation stands, bearing this seal: “The Lord knows those who are His,” and, “Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord must turn away from iniquity.”
You destroy those who tell lies; the LORD abhors the man of bloodshed and deceit.

notes.quote: ἐρεῖ λέγων ὑμῖν, οὐκ οἶδα πόθεν ἐστέ; ἀπόστητε ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ, πάντες ἐργάται ἀδικίας
notes.note: If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [he will reply that he does not know where you are from, and he will tell you to go away because you are evildoers]
In your language, it might seem that this phrase expresses unnecessary extra information. If so, you could abbreviate it. Alternate translation: [he will tell you]
Since the owner of the house is speaking to the people outside, you would be plural in these instances. The implied “you” in the command to get away would also be plural.

notes.note: These are actions that indicate deep regret and sadness. If people in your culture would not express themselves in this way, you could use a general expression. Alternate translation: [actions that express great mourning]

This mystery is that through the gospel the Gentiles are fellow heirs, fellow members of the body, and fellow partakers of the promise in Christ Jesus.

Jesus is using the adjective first as a noun in order to indicate a group of people. ULT adds the word ones to show that. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you could translate this term with an equivalent phrases. Alternate translation: [people who are greatly privileged]

I have glorified You on earth by accomplishing the work You gave Me to do.
“Rabbi, they replied, “the Jews just tried to stone You, and You are going back there?

notes.quote: πορευθέντες εἴπατε τῇ ἀλώπεκι ταύτῃ, ἰδοὺ, ἐκβάλλω δαιμόνια, καὶ ἰάσεις ἀποτελῶ

A fox is a small wild dog. If your readers would not be familiar with what a fox is, you could use the name of a similar animal in your region, or a general expression. Alternate translation: [that little dog]

Jesus is referring to Herod as a fox. This could mean: (1) since foxes need to rely on cunning to catch their prey, Jesus may be saying that Herod is devious. Alternate translation: [that devious person]; (2) since a fox is a small animal, Jesus may be saying that Herod was not much of a threat. Alternate translation: [that insignificant person]
Jesus uses the term Behold to call attention to what he is about to say. Alternate translation: [Indeed]

notes.quote: ἐκβάλλω δαιμόνια, καὶ ἰάσεις ἀποτελῶ σήμερον καὶ αὔριον
notes.note: The expression today and tomorrow is an idiom that means “at the present time” or “for now.” Alternate translation: [for now I will continue to drive out demons and perform healings]

notes.quote: ἐκβάλλω δαιμόνια, καὶ ἰάσεις ἀποτελῶ σήμερον καὶ αὔριον
notes.note: Jesus speaks of two parts of his ministry, driving out demons and performing healings, to mean all of his ministry, which also included teaching and other things. Alternate translation: [for now I will continue to carry on my ministry]

notes.quote: ἐκβάλλω δαιμόνια, καὶ ἰάσεις ἀποτελῶ σήμερον καὶ αὔριον
notes.note: The implication is that Jesus is saying he knows he does not need to be afraid of Herod’s deadly intentions, even though he is in territory that Herod rules, because God will keep him safe while he carries out his ministry. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could state that explicitly. Alternate translation: [I know that for now, with God’s protection, I can safely carry on my ministry even in Herod’s territory]
In this culture, the third day meant “the day after tomorrow.” Jesus is using the expression as an idiom. Alternate translation: [at a short time in the future] or [soon]

If it would be helpful in your language, you could express this with an active form. This could mean: (1) Jesus is saying he will soon complete his work of teaching and healing. Alternate translation: [I will complete my ministry]; (2) this expression refers to someone reaching a goal or destination. Alternate translation: [I will finish traveling through Herod’s territory and reach Jerusalem]; (3) Jesus is referring to a goal or destination, and mean that he will reach the end of his life. Alternate translation: [I will give my life as a sacrifice]; (4) the expression describes someone reaching maturity or perfection of character, and if that is what it means here, it would describe the character that Jesus demonstrated when he gave his life as the Savior. Alternate translation: [I will demonstrate supreme love]

verses.text: Nevertheless, I must keep going today and tomorrow and the next day, for it is not admissible for a prophet to perish outside of Jerusalem.

xrefs.text: But the people there refused to welcome Him, because He was heading for Jerusalem.
The crowds replied, “This is Jesus, the prophet from Nazareth in Galilee.
“Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be delivered over to the chief priests and scribes. They will condemn Him to death
Jesus explained, “My food is to do the will of Him who sent Me and to finish His work.

Then Jesus told them, “For a little while longer, the Light will be among you. Walk while you have the Light, so that darkness will not overtake you. The one who walks in the darkness does not know where he is going.
While it is daytime, we must do the works of Him who sent Me. Night is coming, when no one can work.
The people of Jerusalem and their rulers did not recognize Jesus, yet in condemning Him they fulfilled the words of the prophets that are read every Sabbath.
Jesus answered, “Are there not twelve hours of daylight? If anyone walks in the daytime, he will not stumble, because he sees by the light of this world.

notes.note: Alternate translation: [But I must keep traveling]

notes.quote: σήμερον καὶ αὔριον καὶ τῇ ἐχομένῃ
notes.note: This is an idiom. Alternate translation: [now and in the time just ahead]

notes.quote: οὐκ ἐνδέχεται προφήτην ἀπολέσθαι ἔξω Ἰερουσαλήμ
notes.note: This could also mean “it is not acceptable.” Either way, Jesus is speaking ironically. The Jewish leaders claimed to serve God, and yet their ancestors killed many of God’s prophets in Jerusalem. Jesus knew that they would kill him there too. Alternate translation: [it is in Jerusalem that the Jewish leaders have killed so many of God’s messengers]

named.name: Jerusalem
named.brief: The capital of Israel, a holy city for three religions

verses.text: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets and stones those sent to her, how often I have longed to gather your children together as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, but you were unwilling!

xrefs.text: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets and stones those sent to her, how often I have longed to gather your children together, as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, but you were unwilling!
As an eagle stirs up its nest and hovers over its young, He spread His wings to catch them and carried them on His pinions.
For the Lord GOD, the Holy One of Israel, has said: “By repentance and rest you would be saved; your strength would lie in quiet confidence— but you were not willing.”
Which of the prophets did your fathers fail to persecute? They even killed those who foretold the coming of the Righteous One. And now you are His betrayers and murderers—
As Jesus approached Jerusalem and saw the city, He wept over it
but this is what I commanded them: Obey Me, and I will be your God, and you will be My people. You must walk in all the ways I have commanded you, so that it may go well with you.

This is what the LORD says: “Stand at the crossroads and look. Ask for the ancient paths: ‘Where is the good way?’ Then walk in it, and you will find rest for your souls. But they said, ‘We will not walk in it!’
But the more I called Israel, the farther they departed from Me. They sacrificed to the Baals and burned incense to carved images.

notes.note: Jesus is addressing something he knows cannot hear him, the city of Jerusalem, in order to show his listeners in a strong way how he feels about it. Alternate translation: [I am very upset with the city of Jerusalem] or, if you decide to use the second person (See: later note), [I am very upset with you, Jerusalem]

notes.quote: ἡ ἀποκτείνουσα τοὺς προφήτας, καὶ λιθοβολοῦσα τοὺς ἀπεσταλμένους πρὸς αὐτήν
notes.note: These two phrases mean the same thing. Jesus is likely using repetition for emphasis. If it would be helpful in your language, you could combine the phrases. Alternate translation: [the one killing the prophets God sends her by stoning them]

notes.quote: ἡ ἀποκτείνουσα τοὺς προφήτας, καὶ λιθοβολοῦσα τοὺς ἀπεσταλμένους πρὸς αὐτήν
notes.note: Jesus speaks of the city as if it were female. Your language may customarily use neuter pronouns for cities. Alternate translation: [the one killing the prophets and stoning the ones having been sent to it]

notes.quote: ἡ ἀποκτείνουσα τοὺς προφήτας, καὶ λιθοβολοῦσα τοὺς ἀπεσταλμένους πρὸς αὐτήν
notes.note: If your readers would find it strange that Jesus is addressing the city, you could make it clear that he is really speaking about the people who live in the city: “whose people kill the prophets and stone those sent to them”

notes.quote: ἡ ἀποκτείνουσα τοὺς προφήτας, καὶ λιθοβολοῦσα τοὺς ἀπεσταλμένους πρὸς αὐτήν
notes.note: Jesus speaks of the city in the third person, even though he is addressing it directly. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the second person. Alternate translation: [you who kill the prophets and stone those who are sent to you]

If it would be helpful in your language, you could express this with an active form, and you could state who has done the action. Alternate translation: [those God has sent to her] or [those God has sent to it] or [those God has sent to you]
This is an exclamation and not a question. Alternate translation: [I have desired so often]
Jesus is describing the people who live in Jerusalem as if they were the children of the city. Alternate translation: [to gather your people]

notes.quote: ὃν τρόπον ὄρνις τὴν ἑαυτῆς νοσσιὰν ὑπὸ τὰς πτέρυγας
notes.note: Jesus is leaving out the word gathers that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. you could supply this word from earlier in the sentence. Alternate translation: [the way a hen gathers her own brood under her wings]

Even though Jesus is speaking of the people who live in Jerusalem, he is addressing the city, so your would be singular. The pronoun you would also be a singular pronoun in any case where it is needed in your language as a pronoun for a verb, for example, “you were not willing,” and in the phrase “sent to you,” if you decide to use the second person.

notes.quote: ὃν τρόπον ὄρνις τὴν ἑαυτῆς νοσσιὰν ὑπὸ τὰς πτέρυγας
notes.note: Jesus uses this comparison to describe how he wishes he could care for the people of Jerusalem. Alternate translation: [just as if I were a hen gathering her chicks under her wings]
The term brood refers collectively to all of the young offspring of a bird. Alternate translation: [her chicks]

The implication is that a hen would put her baby chicks there to protect them. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could state that explicitly. Alternate translation: [under her wings to protect them]

named.name: Jerusalem
named.brief: The capital of Israel, a holy city for three religions

verses.text: Look, your house is left to you desolate. And I tell you that you will not see Me again until you say, ‘Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord.’

xrefs.text: Blessed is he who comes in the name of the LORD. From the house of the LORD we bless you.
The ones who went ahead and those who followed were shouting: “Hosanna!” “Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord!”
They took palm branches and went out to meet Him, shouting: “Hosanna!” “Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord!” “Blessed is the King of Israel!”
The crowds that went ahead of Him and those that followed were shouting: “Hosanna to the Son of David!” “Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord!” “Hosanna in the highest!”
For the Israelites must live many days without king or prince, without sacrifice or sacred pillar, and without ephod or idol.
In a little while the world will see Me no more, but you will see Me. Because I live, you also will live.

Then Jesus told them, “For a little while longer, the Light will be among you. Walk while you have the Light, so that darkness will not overtake you. The one who walks in the darkness does not know where he is going.
How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of those who bring good news, who proclaim peace, who bring good tidings, who proclaim salvation, who say to Zion, “Your God reigns!”

notes.note: Jesus uses the term Behold to call attention to what he is about to say. Alternate translation: [Indeed]

Jesus is using the present tense in order to refer to something that will happen in the future. He is doing this to show that the event will certainly happen. Alternate translation: [your house will be left to you alone]
Jesus speaks of the city of Jerusalem as if it were a house in which its people lived. Alternate translation: [your city will be left to you alone]
If it would be helpful in your language, you could express this with an active form, and you could state who will do the action. Alternate translation: [God is going to leave your city to you alone]

The implications of this statement are that God will no longer consider that Jerusalem belongs to him, as a holy city where he dwells in his temple, and that God will therefore not protect the people of Jerusalem from their enemies. Alternate translation: [God will not protect you from your enemies]

Jesus is now speaking directly to the people who live in Jerusalem, so your and you would be plural. The pronoun you would also be a plural pronoun in any case where it is needed in your language as a pronoun for a verb, for example, “you say.”
Jesus says this to emphasize what he is telling the people of Jerusalem. Alternate translation: [I can assure you]

notes.quote: οὐ μὴ με ἴδητέ ἕως ἥξει ὅτε εἴπητε
notes.note: If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this a positive statement. Alternate translation: [the next time you see me, you will say]

The expression it comes means “the time comes.” You could express that in your translation, or, if your language does not speak of time as “coming,” you can use an equivalent expression. Alternate translation: [until the time comes when you say] or [until the time when you say]

notes.quote: ὅτε εἴπητε, εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι Κυρίου
notes.note: If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [when you say that the one who comes in the name of the Lord is blessed]
God’s name represents his power and authority. Alternate translation: [as God’s representative]

named.name: LORD
named.brief: Names or title used to refer to God
